Key Evidence Collected (with direct quotes and citations) Unlambda printing via .x - Official documentation (Madore): - “The `.x` function is the only way to perform output in Unlambda… it has a side effect, namely to print the character x on the standard output (this writing takes place when `.x` is applied). … on no account should `.x` be thought of as something applied to x (and, just to insist, there is no such function as `.` (dot), only `.x` (dot x)). The `r` function is just one instance of the `.x` function, namely when x is the newline character.” URL: http://www.madore.org/~david/programs/unlambda/#print - “The `.x` function is written using two characters. The first character is a period and the second is any character. Nevertheless, `.x` is a single function in Unlambda, and x in this expression is merely a character (read during parsing), not a parameter to the function. The `r` function is exactly equivalent to `.(newline)`. The `.x` function behaves like the `i` (identity) function, with the side effect that it prints the character x (to the standard output) when it is applied.” URL: http://www.madore.org/~david/programs/unlambda/#ref - Whitespace exception (space printing): “Whitespace is ignored in an Unlambda program… except, naturally, between the period and the character in the `.x` function name.” URL: http://www.madore.org/~david/programs/unlambda/#ref - Wikipedia: - “The notation `.x` denotes a function which takes one argument and returns it unchanged, printing the single character x as a side effect when it is invoked. … The function `r` is syntactic sugar for the function that prints a newline character.” URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unlambda#Original_built-in_functions - Chu-Carroll: - “`.` — The ‘.’ operator is actually a meta-operator. ‘`.x`’ is a function which returns its parameter, and prints the character ‘x’.” - “`r` is a shorthand for ‘`.CR`’, where CR is the carriage return character.” URL: https://scienceblogs.com/goodmath/2006/08/11/friday-pathological-programmin-3 Combinators s and i - Official documentation (Madore): - s combinator: “The `s` builtin… takes three arguments, X, Y and Z, and evaluates as does ```XZ`YZ`.” URL: http://www.madore.org/~david/programs/unlambda/#combi - i: “The `i` function: it is simply the identity function… It could be replaced by ```skk`.” URL: http://www.madore.org/~david/programs/unlambda/#combi - Wikipedia (cross-check): - Summaries of k, s, i; identity i implementable as ```skk`.
